newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian premier removed by presidential decree.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian premier removed by presidential decree.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko was removed from his post on Thursday due to illness, the president's press office said -- but a close aide to the premier denied he was sick.

"The president has signed a decree and has appointed First Deputy Prime Minister Vasyl Durdynets as acting prime minister. The reason was Lazarenko's illness," a spokesman for President Leonid Kuchma's office said by telephone. But earlier an aide to Lazarenko said he was in good health.
A spokeswoman for Kuchma's office later read out the decree by telephone, clarifying that Durdynets was appointed acting prime minister "for the time of Pavlo Lazarenko's illness".
It was not clear if the decree meant Lazarenko might be reappointed at some later stage, but his aides said the decree effectively meant Lazarenko had been sacked.
They said he was fine when he met Kuchma earlier in the day and that he had held talks with leaders of striking coal miners on Wednesday.
Western partners of Ukraine have been urging Kuchma to remove Lazarenko for months amid allegations of high-level government corruption and failure to make reforms work.
The prime minister's position has weakened since last week as the pro-Kuchma People's Democratic Party and several groups in parliament have called on the president to sack him.
